title: CG 87 02 13 cassava (Sultan 4): Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: CG 87 02 13 cassava: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: CG 87 02 13 cassava is a cassava variety. About 10 months to harvest, 39.9 t/ha in trials. See its pest ratings and traits.
excerpt: CG 87 02 13 is a registered cassava variety, also sold or known as Sultan 4. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council (NSIC) in 2000 as NSIC 2000 Cv 18. It takes about 10 months from planting to harvest, with 39.9 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Sultan 4, this is the same cassava. The facts below come from the NSIC registry kept by the Bureau of Plant Industry. Compare it with the others in our [cassava variety finder](/crop-varieties/cassava), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for root crops](/land-preparation/root-crop-land-preparation).

items: **Days to harvest:** about 10 months from planting to harvest.
**Yield:** 39.9 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

CG 87 02 13 cassava takes about 10 months from planting to harvest. That is 0.5 months faster than the average of the 42 cassava varieties with a day count, 10.5 months. Count the months from planting, and plan the harvest for a dry stretch when you can.

Its average yield of 39.9 t/ha beats the average of its group, 32.38. It sits in the top quarter of its group. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?

blocks.caption: Reactions in the registry trials, rated under natural field conditions
rows: Took some damage but held up
Took some damage but held up

blocks.text: It showed no weak spot in the ratings on record. Still, a resistant variety can break down when a new strain or pest population comes, so keep scouting.

The pests and diseases that hit cassava fields most often: [whitefly](/pests/whitefly), [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [Cercospora leaf spot](/diseases/cercospora-leaf-spot), [mealybug](/pests/mealybug). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.

Dry matter is 32.6 percent. A higher dry matter cooks mealy and gives processors more flour or starch from each tonne. The starch content is 22.6 percent. Its cyanide level, the HCN content, is medium. A low level is safer for the table, while a high level calls for peeling, soaking and full cooking. It is recommended it is bitter, used only as starch and feeds.
Where and when to plant CG 87 02 13 cassava

The registry recommends it for anywhere in the country. Pick by buyer first. Starch and feed plants pay for yield and starch content, while the table wants a sweet, low cyanide variety that boils soft. A high starch variety needs a buyer within a day of harvest, because the roots spoil fast.

items.q: Is Sultan 4 the same as CG 87 02 13?
items.a: Yes. Sultan 4 is another name for CG 87 02 13, registered as NSIC 2000 Cv 18. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes about 10 months from planting to harvest. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.
The record shows 39.9 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.
The registry recommends it for anywhere in the country. Ask your municipal agriculturist how it has done in your town.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of CG 87 02 13?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
